305.body:
In **הניקוד בתוך הכתיב**, under **ספר מלכים** in [chapter 5 of the Wikisource Introduction to MAM](https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/%D7%95%D7%99%D7%A7%D7%99%D7%98%D7%A7%D7%A1%D7%98:%D7%9E%D7%91%D7%95%D7%90_%D7%9C%D7%9E%D7%A7%D7%A8%D7%90_%D7%A2%D7%9C_%D7%A4%D7%99_%D7%94%D7%9E%D7%A1%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%94/%D7%A4%D7%A8%D7%A7_%D7%94#%D7%A1%D7%A4%D7%A8_%D7%9E%D7%9C%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%9D_(%D7%97%D7%95%D7%A5_%D7%9E%D7%94%D7%A7%D7%98%D7%A2_%D7%94%D7%97%D7%A1%D7%A8_%D7%91%D7%9B%D7%AA%D7%A8)), the pointed ketiv **<ֵשֵׁ֥נַיְֵהֶ֖ם>** at **2 Kings 18:27** includes a shin dot. The Aleppo manuscript is well preserved here and clearly has no dot above shin. Please remove the shin dot from the Introduction's list.

The absence is expected: such a dot would belong only to a hypothetical pointing of the “chanted ketiv”, which is something of an oxymoron.

![Aleppo Codex, 2 Kings 18:27: no dot above shin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/55f45fff37268cb450c32595a5761643c38dcdb2/in/near-aleppo/img/aleppo-2K18-27-shin.png)

Edited by a Codex session on 2026-10-13, at Ben's request, to focus the body on Avi's correction.

Written by a Codex session on 2026-10-13, at Ben's request. The original issue body is preserved below as technical context; the rewritten body presents the correction for Avi.

<details>
<summary>Technical provenance and investigation details</summary>

Written by a Codex session on 2026-10-13. Ben's instruction was: “Create a MAM-basics github issue to sort of do the opposite of what we thought might be needed”. Everything else below is this session's reconstruction, with Ben's manuscript reading attributed explicitly.

The Introduction's list should omit the shin dot in its Aleppo ketiv form at **2 Kings 18:27**. Near-Aleppo should retain its current form without that dot.

### Manuscript evidence

Ben supplied an Aleppo Codex crop and reported on 2026-10-13: “I see no evidence of any kind of dot, shin dot or otherwise, on top of the shin, and the manuscript (Aleppo) is well preserved here, so I feel confident in this result.”

![Aleppo Codex, 2 Kings 18:27: no dot above the ketiv shin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/55f45fff37268cb450c32595a5761643c38dcdb2/in/near-aleppo/img/aleppo-2K18-27-shin.png)

The [tracked screenshot](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/55f45fff37268cb450c32595a5761643c38dcdb2/in/near-aleppo/img/aleppo-2K18-27-shin.png) is an unchanged copy of `Screenshot 2026-10-13 133636.png`. Its SHA-256 is `08b5f95b451c0464f15c85815323baf1a66e8aed58eb63cd7c76dc8915d353b8`. The [investigation record](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/55f45fff37268cb450c32595a5761643c38dcdb2/doc/near-aleppo-avi-ketiv-investigation.html), section “2 Kings 18:27: shin dot”, records Ben's observation, full screenshot provenance, and the reversed disposition. The published [interesting ketiv/qere FOI case](https://bdenckla.github.io/MAM-basics/near-aleppo/foi/interesting-ketiv-qere.html#2-kings-18-27) will display the crop after the normal Pages deployment.

### Source disagreement and proposed correction

The [cached Introduction chapter 5 entry](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/fb5660216b38f2ad93fdfba50eaec9b6940dd6c9/in/mam-ws-intro/ch5.mediawiki#L430), revision **3087740**, includes U+05C1 **HEBREW POINT SHIN DOT** on the ketiv's shin. Both [MAM chapter-note representations](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/fb5660216b38f2ad93fdfba50eaec9b6940dd6c9/out/near-aleppo/plus/BC-Kings.json#L15537) omit that dot, as does the [reviewed near-Aleppo pointing](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/fb5660216b38f2ad93fdfba50eaec9b6940dd6c9/in/near-aleppo/reviewed-pointed-ketiv.json#L1355).

The proposed edit is to remove only U+05C1 from that shin in the Introduction's listed form. Retain all other vowels, accents, and orphan-mark notation. The full pointed forms are in the HTML investigation; the issue identifies the exact edit by code point to avoid GitHub's known transport problems with stacked Hebrew marks.

### Work to complete

- Check the live Introduction's chapter 5 entry for 2 Kings 18:27 and remove the shin dot if it still has the cached form.
- Keep near-Aleppo's current pointing without a shin dot, which agrees with Ben's confident manuscript reading.
- After the source correction, refresh the Introduction's independent local mirror using its [maintained procedure](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/main/in/mam-ws-intro/README.md), and inspect the resulting diff.

This reverses the earlier possible near-Aleppo addition. The observed absence also removes the evidence that prompted Ben's suspicion of pointing for both a hypothetical “pronounced ketiv” and the euphemistic qere at this site. No such mixed-pointing explanation is needed for this case.

</details>

Written by a Codex session on 2026-10-13, at Ben's request.

**The corresponding chapter doc-note needs no correction on the shin-dot point.** At **2 Kings 18:27**, both quoted Aleppo ketiv representations of **שניהם** already omit the shin dot, agreeing with Ben's confirmed manuscript reading. See the [preserved doc-note](https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics/blob/e67573b732546d9ff423bf7b6abca51150b941a7/MAM-parsed/plus/BC-Kings.json#L15856).

The doc-note's prose discusses tsere placement and does not explicitly state that the shin dot is absent. Its disagreement with the Introduction is in the quoted Aleppo forms. I checked the live Wikisource chapter wikitext on 2026-10-13 and confirmed this reading.
